lede: Milk drawn pure from between what is digested and blood. Ships cutting the sea. A bird held up by nothing in the open air. A bee, taught where to build. This surah counts what a human being has been given, twice over, and then stops: “If you tried to number the favours of Allah, you could not count them.”

names.name: al-Naḥl
names.note: After the bee to which Allah gave its instructions (16:68–69): where to make its houses, what to eat, and how to keep to the paths of its Lord.

names.name: Sūrat al-Niʿam
names.note: So it was also called, al-Qurṭubī says, because of the number of His favours upon His servants that Allah counts out in it.

revelation.verdict: Makkan — its closing ayat came later
revelation.detail: Mujāhid, ʿAṭiyyah and Ibn Abī Ṭalḥah relate from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is Makkan, and so it is reported from al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah and ʿAṭāʾ. The exceptions the scholars name cluster at its end: Ibn ʿAbbās said, in one report, that “If you punish, then punish with the like of what you were made to suffer” came down after the killing of Ḥamzah, and al-Shaʿbī held the whole surah Makkan except those last three ayat. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s report places them on the day Makkah was conquered. The traditional order puts the surah seventieth.
revelation.when: The later years in Makkah; its closing ayat after Uḥud

evidence.quote: رَوى مُجاهِدٌ، وعَطِيَّةُ، وابْنُ أبِي طَلْحَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ
وقالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ في رِوايَةٍ: إنَّهُ نَزَلَ مِنها بَعْدَ قَتْلِ حَمْزَةَ: ﴿وَإنْ عاقَبْتُمْ فَعاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ ما عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ
وَتُسَمَّى سُورَةُ النِّعَمِ بِسَبَبِ مَا عَدَّدَ اللَّهُ فِيهَا مِنْ نِعَمِهِ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ

setting: Quraysh used to taunt the Prophet ﷺ about the punishment he warned of: let it come, then. The surah’s first words answer them — “The command of Allah has come; so do not seek to hasten it” — and then it changes the subject entirely. It does not describe the punishment. It describes what they already have.

The first inventory runs from the largest things to the nearest. The heavens and the earth. Man himself, made from a drop, “and there he is, an open disputant.” The cattle: warmth, and food, “and there is beauty in them for you, when you bring them home in the evening and when you drive them out to pasture.” Horses, mules and donkeys, to ride and for show — “and He creates what you do not know.” Rain, and what it grows. The night and the day. The sea, giving fresh meat and ornaments to wear, with the ships ploughing through it. Mountains, rivers, roads, landmarks — “and by the stars they find their way.” Then the question: “Is He who creates like one who does not create?”

The second inventory comes closer still. Milk, “pure and pleasant to those who drink.” The bee: “Your Lord inspired the bee: make houses in the mountains, in the trees, and in what people build; then eat of every fruit, and follow the paths of your Lord made smooth” — and from its belly comes a drink of varying colours, in which there is healing for people. Wives, children and grandchildren. Birds held in the sky. Houses to rest in, and tents of hide that are light to carry on the day of travel. Shade, shelter, and clothing against the heat. The list ends with one of the saddest lines in the Qurʾan: “They recognise the favour of Allah; then they deny it.”

Having established what is owed, the surah says what to do about it, in an ayah Ibn Masʿūd called the most comprehensive in the Qurʾan: “Allah commands justice, and the doing of good, and giving to kinsfolk; and He forbids indecency, wrong and oppression.”

It does not pretend the believers’ situation was easy. It speaks of those who emigrated after being wronged; of the one who is forced to utter disbelief while his heart is at rest in faith; of a town that was secure and at ease, and was ungrateful, and tasted hunger and fear. And its last three ayat, which came down after the bodies of Ḥamzah and the dead of Uḥud had been mutilated, hold the community to a limit in the moment it would be hardest to keep: “If you punish, then punish with the like of what you were made to suffer. But if you are patient — that is better for the patient.”

occasions.title: After Uḥud
occasions.text: “On the day of Uḥud, sixty-four of the Helpers were struck down, and six of the Emigrants, among them Ḥamzah; and they were mutilated. The Helpers said: ‘If we have a day like this against them, we shall outdo them.’ When the day of the conquest of Makkah came, Allah sent down: ‘If you punish, then punish with the like of what you were made to suffer; but if you are patient, that is better for the patient.’ A man said: ‘No Quraysh after today!’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘Hold back from the people, except four.’”
occasions.source: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: al-Tirmidhī (3129); a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ chain according to al-Albānī.

aim: To recall the favours that point to the One who gives them — binding people to worship Him, and warning against the denial of His favour.
themes: The cattle, the sea and the stars
“Is He who creates like one who does not?”
Justice and the doing of good

outline.title: The command has come
outline.summary: The command of Allah has come; so do not seek to hasten it. He sends down the angels with the spirit, by His command, upon whom He wills of His servants. He created man from a drop — and there he is, an open disputant. And the cattle He created for you: in them is warmth and benefit, and of them you eat; and there is beauty in them for you. Horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride, and as adornment; and He creates what you do not know.

outline.title: The first inventory
outline.summary: He it is who sends down water from the sky: from it you drink, and from it grow the trees. He grows for you crops, olives, palms and vines. He has subjected to you the night and the day, the sun and the moon. He it is who subjected the sea, that you may eat from it fresh meat and bring out of it ornaments to wear. He cast firm mountains into the earth, and rivers and roads, and landmarks; and by the stars they find their way. Is He who creates like one who does not create? If you tried to number the favours of Allah, you could not count them (16:18).

outline.title: Those who refuse, and those who accept
outline.summary: When it is said to them, “What has your Lord sent down?” they say, “Tales of the ancients.” Those before them plotted, and the roof fell upon them from above. And it is said to the mindful, “What has your Lord sent down?” They say, “Good.” We raised in every community a messenger: worship Allah, and shun false gods. Those who emigrated for Allah after being wronged. Ask the people of the Reminder, if you do not know. Do they not see how the shadows of all things turn, right and left, prostrating to Allah?

outline.title: Ingratitude
outline.summary: Allah has said: do not take two gods. Whatever favour you have is from Allah; then when harm touches you, to Him you cry; then when He removes it, a party of you associate others with their Lord. They assign daughters to Allah — and when one of them is given news of a female, his face darkens: shall he keep her in disgrace, or bury her in the dust? Were Allah to take people to task for their wrongdoing, He would not leave on the earth a single creature. We sent down the Book to you only that you may make clear to them what they differ over.

outline.title: The second inventory
outline.summary: Allah sends down water from the sky and gives life to the earth after its death. In the cattle there is a lesson: We give you to drink, from between what is digested and blood, pure milk. Your Lord inspired the bee. Allah created you, then takes you; and some of you are returned to the feeblest age. He gave you spouses, and from them children and grandchildren. Do they not see the birds, held in the air of the sky? He made your houses a place of rest, and garments to protect you from the heat. They recognise the favour of Allah; then they deny it.

outline.title: What He commands
outline.summary: The Day We raise from every community a witness. We sent down to you the Book as a clarification of all things. Allah commands justice, the doing of good, and giving to kinsfolk; and He forbids indecency, wrong and oppression. Fulfil the covenant of Allah; do not be like her who untwists her yarn after it was spun strong. What is with you runs out, and what is with Allah remains. Whoever does right, male or female, and is a believer — We shall give them a good life. When you recite the Qurʾan, seek refuge with Allah from Satan.

outline.title: Under pressure
outline.summary: When We put one ayah in place of another, they say, “You are only inventing.” Say: the Holy Spirit brought it down from your Lord in truth. We know they say, “It is only a human being who teaches him” — the tongue of the one they point to is foreign, and this is clear Arabic speech. Whoever disbelieves after believing — except one who is forced, while his heart is at rest in faith. Those who emigrated after they had been persecuted. A town that was secure and at ease, and was ungrateful for the favours of Allah. Eat of what Allah has provided you, lawful and good.

outline.title: Ibrāhīm, and the last counsel
outline.summary: Ibrāhīm was a community in himself, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright; thankful for His favours. Then We revealed to you: follow the creed of Ibrāhīm. Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good counsel, and argue with them in the best manner. If you punish, then punish with the like of what you were made to suffer; but if you are patient, that is better for the patient. Be patient — and your patience is only through Allah. Allah is with those who are mindful, and those who do good.

keyAyah.why: The point at which the counting stops. It closes not with a rebuke for the uncounted favours, but with two names: Forgiving, Merciful.

virtues.text: Ibn Masʿūd said: “The most comprehensive ayah in the Qurʾan is in Sūrat al-Naḥl: ‘Allah commands justice and the doing of good…’”
virtues.source: Al-Ṭabarī, and al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad — quoted by Ibn Kathīr
virtues.grade: A saying of the Companion, not a hadith of the Prophet ﷺ

evidence.quote: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ يَقُولُ: إِنَّ أَجْمَعَ آيَةٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ فِي سُورَةِ النَّحْلِ: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالإحْسَانِ

virtues.text: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “My brother has a complaint of the stomach.” He said: “Give him honey to drink.” He came a second time, and a third, and was told the same. Then he came and said: “I have done so.” He ﷺ said: “Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother’s stomach has lied. Give him honey to drink.” He did, and he was cured.
virtues.arabic: صَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَكَذَبَ بَطْنُ أَخِيكَ اسْقِهِ عَسَلاً

virtuesNote: The fiftieth ayah is an ayah of prostration. The ninetieth — “Allah commands justice and the doing of good” — is the ayah read at the close of the Friday sermon in much of the Muslim world, a practice commonly traced to the caliph ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.
before: Al-Ḥijr ended with the Prophet ﷺ told to worship until the certain end comes. Al-Naḥl opens: the command of Allah has come.
after: Al-Naḥl ends: “Allah is with those who are mindful.” Al-Isrāʾ opens with the greatest sign of that nearness: “Glory be to Him who took His servant by night.”
